newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament clears exports guarantee bill.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament clears exports guarantee bill.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament on Friday passed a bill aimed at improving the country's exports guarantee system.

The draft law would set up a government body called the Credit Insurance Policy Committee, which would devise credit guarantee policies and supervise the Credit Exports Insurance Corporation (KUKE) -- a government agency extending guarantees for foreign trade transactions.
"The bill will speed up the process of granting exports guarantees...because one institution will be responsible for them," KUKE president Krzysztof Jasinski told Reuters. @
The bill, passed in a 341 to three vote with 10 abstentions, now needs to clear the Senate and be signed by the president, neither of whom is expected to oppose.

Jasinski said the bill could pave the way for transferring government-owned shares of several foreign trade companies to KUKE to boost its operations but the decision on the switch rested with the government. @

Last year the then acting foreign trade minister Janusz Kaczurba said the government wanted to endow KUKE with shares now belonging to the Polish Guarantee Fund (PFG) and the International Guarantee Corporation (MKK), two state-owned credit guarantees bodies that are due to be liquidated after bringing substantial losses.
Controversy over these losses were among the reasons for the dismissal of the previous foreign trade minister, Jacek Buchacz, in 1996.
